name: Bambara Groundnut

evidence.quote: The bambara groundnut is a fast growing plant, which requires warm temperatures and does not tolerate freezing temperatures during the growing season.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: The bambara groundnut is propagated by seed.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: It is planted from October to early December after good rainfall.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: A growth period of 110 to 150 days is required for the crop to develop fully. Plants should be harvested when they turn yellow or wilt or when about 80 % of the pods have matured.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Days to pod/seed maturity, not a leaf/vegetable harvest (crop is grown for its underground seed).

harvestPeriodWeeksOrMonths.value: harvested once at maturity; small plots often harvested over a period of time as pods mature/break off unevenly

evidence.quote: Harvesting small plots is often done over a period of time. Bambara pods can break off very easily and up to half of the pods can remain in the soil, requiring collection by hand.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: seed can be planted 2,5 to 3,0 cm deep and 5,0 to 7,5 cm deep in sandy soil, with a recommended spacing of 10 to 15 cm in sin­gle rows of 45 to 90 cm apart
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: a recommended spacing of 10 to 15 cm in single rows of 45 to 90 cm apart
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

evidence.quote: seed can be planted 2,5 to 3,0 cm deep and 5,0 to 7,5 cm deep in sandy soil
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

sowDepthRangeCm.notes: 2.5-3.0cm on heavy/moist soil, 5.0-7.5cm on sandy soil.

varieties.name: MPB51
varieties.note: ARC Lowveld Research Unit local selection bred for higher yields (2355 kg, unit/basis not specified in source).

evidence.quote: Two local variety selection, MPB51 and MPB31 have been developed by the Lowveld Research Unit for higher yields (2355 kg) and high tolerance to A. vogelii respectively.
evidence.doc: Bambara Groundnuts (Vigna subterranea) Production Guideline, DAFF, 2016

varieties.name: MPB31
varieties.note: ARC Lowveld Research Unit local selection bred for high tolerance to the root parasite Alectra vogelii.

varieties.note: Early maturing, usually small to medium-sized kernels, mainly one-seeded.

zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Named major production areas: Limpopo (Mopani, Capricorn, Waterberg, Vhembe districts) and Mpumalanga (Ehlanzeni district, where ARC's Lowveld Research Unit is based).
zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: KwaZulu-Natal areas named: Greytown, Msinga, Nkandla, Nguthuthu, Makhati, Kosibaai, plus minor production in Umzinyathi and Illembe districts.
zoneNotes.highveld: North West and Gauteng are named as major production areas, but the source does not distinguish highveld frost risk for this crop, which it states 'does not tolerate freezing temperatures' (gap: no explicit highveld guidance beyond the general Oct-early Dec window).

gaps: No t/ha (or any per-hectare) yield figure in the source; only one ambiguous 'yields (2355 kg)' note for a specific ARC selection (MPB51) with no stated area basis or units clarified as kg/ha.

Not grown commercially in South Africa per the source ('The crop is not grown commercially in South Africa... little was known about the optimum agronomic practices for this crop'), so recommendations are subsistence-level rather than a full agronomic package.
No winter-rainfall (Western Cape), all-year (subtropical coast) or mild-frost specific sowing windows given beyond the single Oct-early Dec national window.
The 7 landrace seed-colour types are not tied to specific SA growing zones in the source (only stated to be 'location specific' in general).
summary: DAFF's 2016 Bambara Groundnut production guideline gives solid sourcing for climate/frost sensitivity, sowing window, spacing, sowing depth and days-to-maturity, and documents named local ARC selections (MPB51, MPB31) plus 7 landrace seed-colour types. No yield or seed-rate figures are given, and the source itself states the crop is not grown commercially in SA and its optimum agronomy is not well known, so verdict is partial.
